enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer access token can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by OAuth2/OIDC provider docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token for ordinary bearer access tokens unless a one-time artifact is documented.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf, or lack of documented nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7519 §4.1.5; provided docs only explicitly mention exp enforcement for external JWT auth
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing nbf enforcement as a vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer JWT used for JWT-based machine-to-machine authentication can be submitted multiple times; the documentation does not describe jti replay tracking for this flow.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-machine authentication documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated acceptance of the same JWT alone as replay vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: If a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs, Default & special scopes
oidc_jwt.note: This can look like overbroad authorization but is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens require offline_access to be configured and requested.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs, Authorization code and Refresh token grant sections
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token is not a bug unless offline_access was configured and requested.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based machine authentication creates service accounts named from the provider and subject claim, and these accounts may expire based on the input token exp claim.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-machine authentication docs, JWT authentication section
oidc_jwt.note: Identity names may be derived rather than equal to the raw subject claim.

oidc_jwt.description: When an administrator reconfigures the trusted JWKS URL, discovery URL, or selected federated source/provider, tokens from the new trust anchor are accepted by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source Well-known/JWKS configuration docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance under the new admin-configured trust anchor as a substitution vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC discovery and JWKS data for OAuth Sources are fetched when the source is saved and are not automatically re-fetched afterward.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Old metadata persisting until an admin save is expected behavior, not stale-cache vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs, Authorization code section
oidc_jwt.note: A second exchange failure is expected and should be asserted via HTTP status.

oidc_jwt.description: If an OAuth2 provider's Redirect URI field is empty, the first URL used to open the app is saved as the redirect URL.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth2 provider documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Later acceptance of that first-seen redirect URI is by design after auto-persistence; preconfigure redirect URIs in tests.

oidc_jwt.description: RP-initiated logout ends only that application's session by default; the authentik session remains active unless the provider invalidation flow includes a User Logout stage.
oidc_jwt.source: Single Logout / User Logout stage
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat surviving authentik session as stale-session vulnerability under default configuration.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1/I5 JWT validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set a trusted JWT source (Well-known URL, OIDC JWKS URL, or raw JWKS data) and attach that source to the OAuth2 provider. Without selecting Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers on the provider, login_with_jwt will not exercise JWT validation at all.

For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, the input JWT MUST include exp > {{now_epoch}} for the control case and exp < {{now_epoch}} for the attack case. The docs explicitly state externally issued JWTs are rejected when exp is now or in the past.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the attack token. The provided docs only explicitly document exp enforcement for external JWT authentication and do not document nbf enforcement, so a failed future-token test without a control cannot distinguish broken setup from actual freshness enforcement.

For I1 trust-anchor rotation tests, OAuth Source discovery/JWKS data is fetched upon saving the source and no automatic re-fetching is done. After changing the upstream JWKS or discovery document, the fuzzer MUST explicitly re-save or reconfigure the source/provider before expecting new trust material to take effect.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik does not expose a dedicated bound_issuer field in the documented JWT auth flow. Issuer restrictions must be enforced via an Expression policy using request.context["oauth_jwt"]["iss"]. Do NOT assume issuer comparison happens automatically just because a JWKS source is configured.

For I5 audience-binding tests on login_with_jwt, authentik documentation does not describe automatic aud restriction for externally issued JWT authentication beyond provider/client context. The fuzzer SHOULD enforce audience checks with an Expression policy over request.context["oauth_jwt"] and MUST NOT treat acceptance of arbitrary aud as a bug unless such policy or provider-specific audience expectation was configured.

For I5 scope tests, when no scope is requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope value in start_oidc_auth, exchange_code_for_token, login_with_jwt, and token_exchange. Omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives.

For refresh-token tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 a refresh token is only issued when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the client requests offline_access. Do NOT expect refresh_token in exchange_code_for_token responses unless both conditions are met.

For I3 config-change tests involving redirect URI validation, authentik can auto-save the first redirect URI if the provider's Redirect URI field is left empty and a user opens the app. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure redirect URIs explicitly before testing redirect_uri mismatch; otherwise first-use auto-registration changes the baseline and invalidates the test.

Redirect URI matching supports regex when configured by the admin. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the provider uses literal URI entries or regex patterns. A regex-configured provider may intentionally accept multiple redirect URIs; do not flag that as a mismatch bug.

For I3 authorization-code replay/coherence tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer MUST reuse the exact same code in the replay attempt and compare HTTP status, not identity fields, because the second exchange should fail before any session is created.

For I5 token introspection tests, the introspection endpoint only allows introspecting a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless the token is first exchanged for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspect_token with matching client credentials or perform token_exchange first; cross-provider introspection failure is by design.

For I4 identity-collision tests on login_with_jwt, authentik creates service accounts for JWT authentication based on the provider name and the subject claim of the token. Different providers can therefore intentionally namespace identities by provider. Cross-provider identity differences are expected unless the same provider is used.

For I4 multi-identity tests, the service-account naming scheme for JWT authentication is derived from provider name plus subject claim. The fuzzer MUST keep provider constant when testing whether two different sub values collapse to one identity; changing provider changes the namespace and confounds the result.

For I5 claim-based authorization tests using Expression policies, claim access is through request.context["oauth_jwt"] and requested scopes through request.context["oauth_scopes"]. The fuzzer MUST configure policies against these exact context objects; otherwise tests may pass or fail for unrelated reasons.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on JWT claims, the docs do not specify cross-type comparison semantics for Expression policy evaluation. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly by binding an integer-valued policy check and sending a float claim value (for example 100.7 vs 100) to detect silent truncation or coercion.

For OIDC authorization endpoint tests, start_oidc_auth MUST use content_type=query and MUST NOT follow redirects. The authorization endpoint is browser-mediated and returns redirects as part of normal operation.

For token endpoint operations, exchange_code_for_token, login_with_jwt, token_exchange, introspect_token, and revoke_session MUST use application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies. The docs show form-encoded requests for OAuth token, device, introspection, and revocation style endpoints.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against JWT M2M login, authentik's documented built-in checks for externally issued JWTs only guarantee signature verification against selected Federated OIDC Sources and rejection when exp is now or in the past. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume iss or aud are enforced by default. To test issuer or audience binding, attach an Expression policy that explicitly checks request.context['oauth_jwt']['iss'] and/or other claims; otherwise a passing login may simply reflect unconfigured validation, not a vulnerability.

For I1 trust-anchor and key-rotation tests, JWT trust is configured by selecting Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers. Any JWT signed by any selected source/provider is accepted. The fuzzer MUST isolate tests to a single trusted source/provider unless it intentionally tests multi-trust behavior; otherwise acceptance under another still-selected trust anchor is by configuration, not a bypass.

For I2 expired_token tests on login_with_jwt, authentik explicitly checks exp and rejects tokens whose exp is set as now or in the past. Use a control token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} plus an attack token with exp={{now_epoch_minus_60}}. Without the control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken provider/source setup.

For I2 future_token and nbf tests on login_with_jwt, the documentation only explicitly states exp validation for externally issued JWTs and does not document nbf enforcement. The fuzzer SHOULD include a valid control token and MUST treat acceptance of a token with future nbf as potentially spec-compliant unless separate documentation confirms nbf checking.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, authentik's JWT M2M flow for externally issued JWTs documents signature and exp checks but does not document jti replay tracking. The fuzzer MUST treat repeated use of the same valid bearer JWT as by-design unless the tested artifact is a one-time authorization code. Do not report replay of the same JWT alone as a vulnerability.

For I3 config-change tests involving OAuth Source Well-known or JWKS URL, authentik fetches discovery/JWKS data upon saving the source and performs no automatic re-fetching. The fuzzer MUST explicitly save/update the source configuration to refresh keys/endpoints; waiting alone will not apply new discovery metadata.

For I3 key-rotation tests using a JWKS URL source, authentik stores fetched JWKS data in the source. Because no automatic re-fetching is done, a changed upstream JWKS will not affect validation until the source is saved again. The fuzzer MUST trigger a source update/save before expecting new keys to take effect.

For I3 authorization-code coherence tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer MUST use the same code exactly once for the baseline exchange and obtain a fresh code for any subsequent control sequence. Reusing a code after a successful exchange is expected failure, not a bug.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, authentik validates redirect URIs against the provider's configured Redirect URI list, and those entries may be literal URIs or regexes. The fuzzer MUST know which mode is configured: a regex entry can intentionally match multiple callbacks. Do not treat acceptance of multiple redirect URIs as a bug when the admin configured a regex that matches them.

Redirect URI matching supports regex when the admin configures regex instead of a literal URL. For security tests that require exact redirect_uri binding, the fuzzer MUST configure a literal redirect URI, not a regex. Otherwise broader matches are by design and can create false positives for redirect_uri mismatch or request-object parameter injection tests.

When the provider Redirect URI field is left empty, authentik saves the first URL used to open the app as the redirect URL. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure redirect URIs explicitly before running OIDC security tests. Otherwise first-use auto-saving can make a malicious or unexpected redirect URI become authorized by design.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, authentik treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. The fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope set in baseline and attack requests. Omitting scope broadens requested claims by design and will invalidate least-privilege conclusions.

For refresh-token tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 the refresh token grant requires the offline_access scope, and applications only receive a refresh token when both the application requests offline_access and the provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping. The fuzzer MUST configure both sides before expecting refresh_token issuance or refresh grant success.

For I5 token content tests, values returned in access_token and id_token are controlled by scope mappings. Claims beyond standard defaults may appear because the provider was configured to include them. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged or granted claims against the configured scope mappings and requested scopes, not against generic OIDC expectations.

For introspection tests, authentik documents that you can only introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, unless you first exchange the token for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests with the same provider context as the token under test; cross-provider introspection failure is expected behavior, not a token invalidity signal.

For cross-provider JWT audience tests, authentik-issued JWT federation requires that input JWTs be valid access tokens issued by configured Federated OIDC Providers. The fuzzer MUST ensure provider federation is intentionally configured between the source provider and target provider before testing cross-provider acceptance; otherwise rejection may simply reflect missing federation configuration rather than audience enforcement.

For externally issued JWT M2M tests, the JWT must be signed by certificates from selected Federated OIDC Sources and must not be expired. The fuzzer MUST configure the OAuth2 provider to authenticate against the intended source before submitting client_assertion. Without that selection, failures are setup errors, not security outcomes.

For Entra ID sourced JWT M2M tests, the upstream token must be requested with scope=api://<application_client_id>/.default rather than a Graph scope, otherwise the JWT format is invalid for authentik's JWT authentication. The fuzzer MUST use the application ID URI scope when minting Entra tokens for login_with_jwt controls or attacks.

For I1/I5 audience-binding tests against authentik as an RP consuming external JWTs, the fuzzer MUST configure the OAuth2 provider to select the intended Federated OIDC Source(s). Authentik accepts JWTs signed by any selected source certificates; without isolating sources/providers, cross-source acceptance can be a configuration artifact rather than an audience-validation failure.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired-token tests on JWT M2M login, the attack sequence MUST include a control login using a valid JWT with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Authentik documents only that input JWTs are checked for signature trust and that exp must not be now or in the past; without a control, a generic token error cannot be distinguished from broken source/provider setup.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired-token tests on authentik-issued subject JWTs used for federation, include a control login with a valid unrevoked token. Authentik requires input JWTs to be valid access tokens issued by configured Federated OIDC Providers, not revoked, and not expired; failures otherwise are ambiguous setup errors.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> authentik-issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 trust-anchor rotation tests using Well-known or OIDC JWKS URL on OAuth Sources, the fuzzer MUST account for the fact that discovery/JWKS data is fetched upon saving the source and no automatic re-fetching is done. After changing the upstream JWKS/discovery document, authentik will not pick up the new keys until the source is saved again; do not interpret continued acceptance/rejection before re-save as a cache-coherence bug.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source -> OpenID Connect -> Well-known / JWKS

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences involving source discovery or JWKS changes, NEW logins are evaluated against the source configuration last fetched at save time. A valid coherence test must explicitly re-save/update the source after changing Well-known/JWKS content; otherwise stale behavior is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source -> OpenID Connect -> Well-known / JWKS

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, authentik validates redirect URIs against the provider configuration. If the provider Redirect URI field is empty, authentik saves the first URL a user opens for that app as the redirect URL. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure explicit redirect URIs for deterministic tests; otherwise first-use auto-registration can make a mismatched redirect appear valid by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Redirect URI matching in authentik supports either explicit redirect URLs or administrator-supplied regular expressions. For redirect-uri security tests, the fuzzer MUST know which mode is configured: regex patterns are intentionally broader than exact URLs, and '.' is regex wildcard unless escaped as '\.'. Do not treat regex-authorized redirects as redirect validation bypasses.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope-escalation tests, when no scope is requested authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. The fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope set in baseline and attack requests; omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Default & special scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For refresh-token and offline-access tests, authentik 2024.2+ only returns refresh tokens when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the request includes the offline_access scope. The fuzzer MUST configure both sides; absence of refresh_token otherwise is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code / Refresh token grant / Create OAuth2 provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope-authorization tests, authentik by default allows every user with access to an application to request any configured scopes. Restricting scopes requires an expression policy bound to the application. The fuzzer MUST add such a policy before expecting scope denial; otherwise expanded scopes are by-design behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Scope authorization

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 device-code polling tests, the device authorization response includes expires_in and interval, and polling before user approval returns error=authorization_pending. The fuzzer MUST respect the documented polling interval and token lifetime; aggressive polling or polling after expiry can fail for protocol reasons unrelated to security invariants.
oidc_jwt.source: Device code flow

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 authorization-code replay tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer MUST capture and reuse the exact same code in the replay attempt; obtaining a fresh code after config changes is a different flow and not a replay test.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Authorization code

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC request-object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), authentik documentation only states support for the optional request parameter on the authorization endpoint but does not document request-object signature policy knobs. The fuzzer SHOULD treat acceptance/rejection as endpoint behavior only and MUST NOT assume a missing admin setting exists to require signed request objects.
oidc_jwt.source: Authorization endpoint glossary + required OIDC endpoint extraction context

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1/I5 tests using token introspection, authentik documents that you can only introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, unless you first exchange the token for one from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests with the matching provider context; cross-provider introspection failures are by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> OAuth introspection endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 identity-collision tests on JWT M2M authentication, authentik creates service accounts based on the provider name and the subject claim of the presented token. The fuzzer MUST vary provider and sub independently when testing collisions, because same-sub across different providers is expected to produce different service-account names while repeated use of the same provider+sub is expected to target the same derived account.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> JWT authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests on JWT M2M authentication, externally issued JWTs are only documented to require trusted signature and exp not in the past; no jti replay tracking is documented. The fuzzer MUST NOT flag successful reuse of the same still-valid bearer JWT as a replay vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication -> Externally issued JWTs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 claim-surface tests against UserInfo or tokens, claims returned depend on requested scopes and scope mappings. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes explicitly (for example email, profile, entitlements, offline_access) before asserting claim presence or absence; missing claims without scope are not authorization failures.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider -> Default & special scopes / Provider property mappings

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 logout/session tests, RP-initiated logout in authentik by default only ends that application's session while the authentik session remains active unless the default-provider-invalidation-flow is modified to include a User Logout stage. The fuzzer MUST distinguish provider-session logout from global-session logout to avoid false stale-session findings.
oidc_jwt.source: Single Logout / User Logout stage / OAuth2 front-channel and back-channel logout

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 admin-termination tests, back-channel logout is the only documented mechanism that guarantees provider logout when a session is administratively terminated. If back-channel logout is not configured on the OIDC provider, the fuzzer MUST NOT expect downstream RP sessions to terminate on admin session deletion.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth2 front-channel and back-channel logout / Single Logout

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1/I2 OIDC RP validation tests against external OAuth/OIDC sources, authentik documentation exposes Authorization URL, Access Token URL, Profile URL, and OIDC JWKS URL configuration, but does not document nonce/aud/iss validation toggles. The fuzzer SHOULD test these validations empirically, but MUST treat missing configuration knobs as absence of documented hardening controls rather than setup failure.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source / Entra ID OAuth source

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
